The customization is live today and works for agents like the code reviewer. If you looked, you'd see your project now recognized and using your personalized agent settings instead of the standard ones.

eli5.text: The assistant's behind-the-scenes tool-handling system was rebuilt to be more consistent and less error-prone, but you wouldn't notice any difference in how it behaves. Internally, the way the assistant reads and acts on the tools it's allowed to use (like searching files or running commands) has been reorganized so each tool gets stricter, clearer instructions, which should make future updates safer and less likely to break things. Some configuration was also moved and cleaned up, but again, nothing you can see or do differently has changed yet.

ai.title: Refactor backend tool handler types
ai.summary: Updated `CodebuffToolHandlerFunction` in `backend/src/tools/constants.ts` to enforce `{ result: string; state: Record<string, any> }` returns. Replaced `extra` parameter with direct `requestClientToolCall` and `state` props across handlers like `add-subgoal.ts` and `browser-logs.ts`. Moved `find_files` to `WIP_TOOLS` and deleted its handler file.

eli5.text: I changed how the internal system passes information between its steps so each step now returns a consistent format: a text result plus an optional state for the next step. Handlers that previously received an extra settings object now get their request and state as direct inputs, and one tool, find_files, was moved into a not-ready category and its working file removed. For anyone observing the backend today, tool steps will consistently produce a result string and structured state rather than mixed return shapes; the find_files capability is temporarily unavailable internally. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that does not change what end users see, but standardizes how the system talks to itself between steps.

ai.title: Refactor tool handler signature to use previousToolCallFinished
ai.summary: CodebuffToolHandlerFunction now accepts `previousToolCallFinished` (Promise<void>) instead of `previousToolCallResult` (Promise<any>). Handlers return `{ result: Promise<string>; state: Record<string, any> }` synchronously, chaining result generation via `.then()` on the completion promise. This change decouples tool execution from result retrieval, affecting core tool handlers like `add-subgoal`, `browser-logs`, `code-search`, `end-turn`, `run-file-change-hooks`, `run-terminal-command`, and `update-subgoal`.

eli5.text: The part of the system that runs your coding tasks now waits for one task to fully finish before starting the next, instead of grabbing the previous task's full output and carrying it around. You, as someone using the agent, won't see a different result from your tasks today, but behind the scenes each tool step now signals completion with a simple 'done' flag and passes only what it needs for the next step, rather than the entire prior result. This is live and active across the main task handlers like adding a subgoal, searching code, running commands, and ending a turn.

ai.summary: Corrected logic in `loopAgentSteps` within `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts` to prevent infinite looping of the initial assistant message. The fix introduces a toggle for `currentAssistantMessage` and adjusts the conditional check for `currentAssistantPrefix` to ensure proper state progression. This change ensures that the agent loop correctly alternates between injected step messages and empty states, resolving the hang.

eli5.text: When the system tried to walk through a series of steps, it could get stuck showing you the same opening message over and over instead of moving on. The fix makes it flip back and forth: show the step message once, then show nothing, then show the next step message, and so on. If you were watching it hang or repeat itself, you would now see it keep progressing through the steps instead of looping. This is already live in the product.

ai.title: Add programmatic agent template support
ai.summary: Added support for programmatic agent templates, allowing agents to be defined via code generators instead of LLM prompts. The `runAgentStep` function now detects `implementation === 'programmatic'` and delegates to `runProgrammaticAgent`, which executes a generator function and handles yielded tool calls. Programmatic templates bypass the standard override mechanism in `getAgentTemplateWithOverrides`. An `example_programmatic` agent was added to `agent-list.ts` to demonstrate the new interface.

eli5.text: Developers can now define AI assistants using actual code instead of relying solely on text prompts that another AI interprets. When a code-defined assistant is used, the system runs its built-in generator function directly and processes tool calls step-by-step, bypassing the usual prompt-based override process. An example code-defined assistant was added to demonstrate this new approach, so you would see it listed among the available assistant types. This is live today for internal and developer use.

ai.summary: AGENT_PERSONAS in common/src/constants/agents.ts now combines name and title into a single name field (e.g., 'Buffy the Enthusiastic Coding Assistant'). toolRenderers in npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts skips rendering for unknown agent types by returning null instead of falling back to the raw agentType or 'Agent'. This affects agent name display in tool call outputs.

eli5.text: When you see an assistant's name in the tool output area, it now shows as a single, friendlier label like 'Buffy the Enthusiastic Coding Assistant' instead of a separate name and title. The program also now hides any assistant entry whenever it encounters an unrecognized assistant type, rather than showing a generic 'Agent' label or falling back to a raw code name. This makes the display cleaner and avoids confusing half-labels when something doesn't match the expected list.

ai.title: Agent template tests use id field instead of type
ai.summary: Test mocks and assertions for agent templates switched from `type` to `id` to match the loader's field schema. Covers `dynamic-agent-loader.test.ts` and `agent-overrides.test.ts` in the backend. Ensures validation checks `templates.<name>.id` during template loading.

eli5.text: When the system loads an agent template (like the brainstormer or reviewer helper), its test checks and mock data now look for the template's identity under an 'id' field instead of a 'type' field. If you peeked at the test files, the mock template objects would show 'id': 'brainstormer' rather than 'type': 'brainstormer', and the assertions confirm the loaded template exposes that 'id'. It's an internal test correction so the fake templates match what the real loading code expects, with no change to what users see.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.430
ai.summary: Release package version incremented from 1.0.429 to 1.0.430 in npm-app/release/package.json. Routine version update for the codebuff package.

eli5.text: The software you use just got a fresh packaged release that bundles together fixes and new options that were finished over the past few days. Updating installs the latest version, which includes a smoother startup for analytics (it no longer breaks if tracking settings are missing), a new way to let the assistant use specialized mini-expert helpers instead of the default ones, and cleaner handling of AI tool interactions. It also drops the old Anthropic routing path in favor of routing through OpenRouter, adds a couple of new assistant helper types, and tidies up the behind-the-scenes development commands. The version label itself is the only thing this particular update changed; the user-visible improvements were already built and are now shipped under this version.

ai.title: Add strreplace tool handler
ai.summary: New `str_replace` tool handler added to backend, enabling precise string replacement in files. Handler registered in `codebuffToolHandlers` and removed from `WIP_TOOLS`. Shared `postStreamProcessing` logic extracted from `write-file.ts` to support both `write_file` and `str_replace`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now make targeted edits to specific parts of a file instead of rewriting the whole thing or inserting changes at the end. This works the same way the existing write tool does, so the assistant can both create files and surgically replace text within them. The feature is live today for any workflow that already used the write tool, and no new opt-in is required.

ai.title: Activate readdocs tool backend handler
ai.summary: Implemented `handleReadDocs` in `backend/src/tools/handlers/read-docs.ts` and registered it in `codebuffToolHandlers` within `backend/src/tools/constants.ts`. Removed `read_docs` from `WIP_TOOLS` to enable the feature. The handler integrates with `fetchContext7LibraryDocumentation`, enforcing strict state validation for `userId`, `agentStepId`, and `repoId` before execution. Includes telemetry logging for duration and token estimates.

eli5.text: If you asked the assistant to look up documentation for a specific library or topic, it can now actually do that by pulling in real reference material from an external documentation source. Behind the scenes, the assistant checks that all the required internal identifiers (user, step, and project) are present and correctly matched before fetching anything, logs how long it takes and roughly how much it used, and only then returns the relevant docs to you. This is live today: the documentation lookup feature is turned on and wired into the backend, so anyone who triggers it gets real results instead of a placeholder or error.

ai.title: Promote readfiles from WIP to active backend tool
ai.summary: The `read_files` tool moves from the `WIP_TOOLS` blocklist to the active `codebuffToolHandlers` registry in `backend/src/tools/constants.ts`. A new handler `backend/src/tools/handlers/read-files.ts` implements the logic, delegating to `getFileReadingUpdates` and rendering results via `renderReadFilesResult`. The tool handler signature now requires a `fileContext: ProjectFileContext` parameter, enabling direct access to file system state and token callers.

eli5.text: Starting July 10, 2025, the assistant gained the ability to read files you point it to as an active tool, previously it was restricted to a work-in-progress list. When the assistant selects this feature, it directly accesses your project files and returns their contents to you in the conversation. You would notice this when the assistant reads a file and shows you its contents without needing manual copy and paste. This change affects all users interacting with the assistant where file reading is supported.

ai.title: Add git worktree init and cleanup scripts with port overrides
ai.summary: Added `init-worktree.ts` and `cleanup-worktree.sh` scripts to manage git worktrees with isolated environments. New `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_PORT` env var in `packages/internal/src/env.ts` and dynamic port usage in `web/package.json` dev script enable port overrides. Root `package.json` exposes `init-worktree` and `cleanup-worktree` commands.

eli5.text: The development team added a pair of helper commands that let a developer spin up a separate, isolated copy of the project for testing a feature without disturbing anyone else's work, and tear it down again when they are done. Each isolated copy can run on its own custom port numbers, so multiple test versions can run side by side. If you browse to the repository today, you will see two new one-line commands in the project's main instruction list that launch these setup and cleanup helpers. The underlying machinery is in place and wired up, so running the new commands will create and destroy these isolated workspaces as described.
